title: Opinions and suggestions
lead: Is lesson ke baad tum design, timeline ya feature par apni opinion English me de sakte ho, politely disagree kar sakte ho, aur better option suggest kar sakte ho.
description: Week 11 English lesson: give an opinion, agree and disagree politely, and suggest a better option in a meeting.

patterns.say: I think the blue design looks better.
patterns.positive: I think the blue design looks better.
patterns.negative: I don't think we need a new logo.
patterns.question: What do you think?
examples: I think we should start with the homepage.
Mujhe lagta hai humein homepage se shuru karna chahiye.
I don't think the price is too high.
Mujhe nahi lagta price zyada hai.
patterns.grammar: I think + clause. Negative often I don't think + clause, not I think not.
patterns.mistake: “I think that is better design” → “I think the blue design is better.” Clear subject rakho.

patterns.note: Thoda formal opinion — meetings ke liye.
patterns.say: In my opinion, we should start with the homepage.
patterns.positive: In my opinion, we should start with the homepage.
patterns.negative: In my opinion, this isn't the right time.
patterns.question: What's your opinion?
examples: In my opinion, the simpler design is better.
Mere hisaab se simple design better hai.
In my opinion, we need more testing.
Mere hisaab se humein zyada testing chahiye.
patterns.grammar: In my opinion, + clause. Comma ke baad complete sentence.
patterns.mistake: “In my opinion is better” → “In my opinion, it is better.” Opinion ke baad clause chahiye.

patterns.say: Why don't we start with the homepage?
patterns.positive: Why don't we start with the homepage?
patterns.negative: Why don't we wait for the feedback?
patterns.question: Why don't we meet on Monday?
examples: Why don't we ask the client?
Client se kyun nahi poochhte?
Why don't we test it first?
Pehle test kyun nahi karte?
patterns.grammar: Why don't we + base verb = suggestion. Real question nahi, idea hai.
patterns.mistake: “Why we don't start?” → “Why don't we start?” Question word + don't + subject.

patterns.say: I agree with you, but I'm not sure about the timeline.
patterns.question: Do you agree?
examples: I agree with your point.
Main aapki baat se sehmat hoon.
I'm not sure about the price.
Main price ke baare me sure nahi hoon.
patterns.grammar: agree with + person; agree to + plan; agree on + decision. I'm not sure = polite disagreement.
patterns.mistake: “I am agree” → “I agree.” Agree khud verb hai, isliye am nahi.

patterns.say: What if we use a simpler design?
patterns.positive: What if we use a simpler design?
patterns.negative: What if we don't change it?
patterns.question: What if we ask the client?
examples: What if we test both options?
Kya hum dono options test karein?
What if we move the deadline?
Kya hum deadline aage badhayein?
patterns.grammar: What if + subject + present simple = suggestion/possibility.
patterns.mistake: “What if we will use” → “What if we use.” If clause me present simple.

patterns.note: Idea accept karna, short aur natural.
patterns.question: Does that sound good?
examples: That sounds good. Let's do it.
Ye achha lagta hai. Chalo karte hain.
That sounds expensive.
Ye mehnga lagta hai.
patterns.mistake: “That sounds well” → “That sounds good.” Sound ke baad adjective.

grammarRules: I think the blue design is better.
In my opinion, we should start small.
Why don't we ask the client?
agree with person / agree to plan
I agree with you. I agree to the plan.
mistakes: In my opinion, it is better.
What if we will use a simpler design?
What if we use a simpler design?
I think that is better design.
I think the blue design is better.

dialogue.context: Design meeting. Riya = client. Opinion, polite disagreement aur better option — teeno use karo.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: We have two designs. Which one do you prefer?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I think the blue design looks better. It feels more professional.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: I'm not sure. The orange one is more visible.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: That's a good point. What if we use blue for the header and orange for the button?

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.text: That sounds good. Should we test both with users?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I agree. In my opinion, a small test is better than a long debate.

dialogue.closing: Opinion ka formula: I think + reason. Disagreement ka formula: That's a good point + What if we...?

speakPrompts.title: 2. Disagree politely
speakPrompts.prompt: Sehmat na ho, but softly bolo.
speakPrompts.starter: That's a good point, but I'm not sure about ___ . What if we ___ ?

speakPrompts.title: 3. Suggest an option
speakPrompts.starter: Why don't we ___ ? What if we ___ ?

speakPrompts.title: 4. Close with agreement
speakPrompts.starter: That sounds good. I agree with ___ . Let's ___ .

vocab.example: In my opinion, the design is clean.
The blue design is a better option.
I politely disagree with that point.
Maybe we should test it first.
Is it possible to finish by Friday?

selfCheck: Formal version “In my opinion, ___” use ki.
Ek suggestion “Why don't we ___?” se di.
Politely disagree kiya — “I'm not sure about ___”.
Agreement “That sounds good” se close kiya.

pronunciation.title: Contrastive stress
pronunciation.body: I think the BLUE design is better, not the ORANGE one. Contrast wale word par stress.

pronunciation.title: Softening
pronunciation.body: I'm not sure — voice soft, slow. “I disagree” se zyada polite lagta hai.

pronunciation.title: Linking
pronunciation.body: What if → /wɒtɪf/. Why don't we → /waɪdəʊntwi/. Suggestions me words jodo.

pronunciation.title: I think
pronunciation.body: Fast speech me “I think” halka hota hai: /aɪ θɪŋk/. Har word par stress mat do.

followUps: Meeting me politely disagree karne ka best phrase kya hai?
“I think” aur “In my opinion” me kya difference hai?
Client ke idea ko reject karna ho to kaise bolun?
Meri suggestion confident lag rahi hai ya unsure?
Decision close karne ka best line kya hai?
mission: Say one opinion in English in a real meeting — I think ___ because ___.
